title: overnight-interview-tally - Arjun Patel
body:
Candidate: Elie Navarro
Role: Senior Runtime Engineer (inference runtime)
Interview date: 2024-10-18 (late panel)
Interviewers: Maya Singh (lead), Dana Ortiz (infra), Leo Park (serving runtime)
Context: Final on-site loop-ish but remote; candidate comes from small infra-heavy startup and a distributed systems research lab. Looking for take: can they own production-facing KV/caching, quantization rollout, and be first-line for Dedicated reliability work.

Purpose of this note
- Rapid tally of signals to aid final hiring council. Not polished: snapshots, counterfactuals, and a short recommended next step.

Quick headline (TL;DR)
- Strengths: solid systems mental model, pragmatic tradeoffs, clear ownership instincts. Good at instrumentation-first approaches and phased rollouts.
- Concerns: low exposure to some of our ecosystem (TensorRT-like stacks and multi-model routing), occasional surface-level answers to kernel selection questions. Hasn't shipped at multi-tenancy Dedicated scale but has applicable infra experience.
- Recommendation: hire with strong reference check + 2-week pairing trial (paid) focused on a real infra task (KV cache eviction policy experiment).

Competency scoring (1-5, with short notes)
- Systems design & capacity planning: 4
  - Gave a clear approach for sizing GPU pools for mixed sequence workloads: percentile-based SLA planning + simulation loop. Proposed a synthetic traffic generator to exercise tails. Good practical examples from past job.
- Production debugging & incident triage: 5
  - Fast at isolating root cause in a mock outage we discussed (cache stampede vs kernel OOM). Suggested quick mitigations (circuit breaker, degrade to smaller model variant) and a postmortem checklist.
- Model-serving internals (KV cache, attention state): 3
  - Understands high-level KV caching and how to reduce repeated prefix work. When probed on exact memory layout and perf implications of different cache representations (compressed vs raw tensors), answers were plausible but not deep on CUDA/kernel intricacies.
- Observability and metrics: 5
  - Strong: advocated token-level latency histograms, per-model cost attribution, and synthetic evals tied to quality monitors. Suggested concrete dashboards and alerting thresholds.
- Team & communication: 5
  - Articulate, candid with tradeoffs, good at writing memos (provided an example he authored). Comfortable with stakeholder communication.

Notes from question threads (raw)
1) KV cache eviction policy (scenario probe)
- Q: You have limited GPU memory for KV cache across many simultaneous conversations. How do you decide eviction policy?
- Candidate: layered approach — hot set per-token-frequency, LRU per-conversation, and cross-conversation scoring using recency * estimated future probability (simple predictive model trained on traffic). Suggested fallback: prefix-anchoring for high-value customers. Also suggested maintaining a compact Bloom-filter-like summary for quick membership checks.
- My note: Good practical multi-tier idea. Implementation complexity moderate. Need to probe if they can implement in C++/CUDA or only in Python and orchestration layer.

2) Model variant fallback and routing (design probe)
- Candidate recommended a policy-driven router: prioritize latency SLO -> region locality -> cost. For overload, automatic downgrade to a quantized variant with a bounded quality delta and canary rollout.
- Follow-up: asked about how to measure "bounded quality delta" in prod. Candidate proposed periodic A/B evals with short prompt sets and a bounded short-term rollback automation. Reasonable.

3) Kernel selection & quantization tradeoffs (deep probe)
- Candidate described quantization pipeline, post-training static quantization, and per-layer outlier correction. On specifics of kernel selection for a given attention block shape on A100 vs H100, candidate deferred to specialized team and suggested benchmarking harness.
- My note: not fatal but indicates we should pair them with someone senior on kernel work if hired.

4) Incident roleplay: spike in tail latency from context windows increasing by 3x
- Candidate suggested immediate mitigation: reduce max_context on the router per-tenant, enable aggressive batching windows, and temporality scale-up of burst capacity. Proposed long-term: background garbage-collection of cached prefixes and re-evaluate kernel memory usage.
- My note: rapid and pragmatic; puts customer availability first.

Concrete things candidate did well (green flags)
- Came prepared with a one-pager describing an "eviction-experiment" they ran at previous employer (included simulation and real workload results). Practical thinking about measuring impact (p99/p999 latency, token-cost delta).
- Strong on alerting and postmortem culture. Suggested straightforward runbooks and automation to reduce alert fatigue.
- Comfortable writing infra proposals and soliciting cross-team feedback. Provided an example GitHub RFC.

Concerning signals (red flags)
- Limited low-level GPU/kernel tuning depth. Mentions "delegate to infra" on kernel micro-optimizations. For our repo of fast kernels this could be a ramp issue.
- Limited direct experience with multi-tenant Dedicated fleets at 100s of GPUs; previous role was smaller but with similar complexity in edge infra.
- Small hesitation on complex quantization failure modes (activation range collapse) when pushed; would need time with our applied-ML folks.

Suggested follow-ups (actionable)
- Short paid pairing trial (2 weeks, paid) with assignment: implement a prototype eviction policy for the KV cache in our staging harness, including load generator and metrics dashboard. Deliverable: code change + runbook + short writeup of results. Owner: Maya to draft assignment doc.
- Reference check: ask specifically about kernel-level contributions and scale of fleet they worked on. Owner: Dana.
- Pairing session with our applied-ML engineer (1 hour deep dive) to probe quantization experience. Owner: Leo to schedule.

Decision recommendation for panel
- Move to offer contingent on passing the pairing trial and reference verification. Target level: Senior (IC4) with path to Principal if they upskill kernel work in 6 months.

Suggested onboarding / 30-60-90 plan (if hired)
- 0-30 days: ramp on serving runtime codebase, complete a small bugfix in the KV cache and add an instrumentation metric (token-level hits/misses). Pair with Maya.
- 30-60 days: land the eviction-policy prototype from the trial into a controlled canary; write runbook and alerting thresholds; coordinate with hosting team for Dedicated capacity tests.
- 60-90 days: lead a cross-team postmortem on the initial canary and iterate; propose a path for kernel optimizations or a vendor benchmark run.

Open questions to resolve in follow-ups
- Can they commit to C++/CUDA changes when necessary (not just orchestration)?
- How comfortable are they with writing microbenchmarks that target attention kernel shapes?
- References should confirm the scale of fleet and whether they owned low-level perf code.

Loose transcript excerpts (paraphrased)
- On eviction heuristics: "I prefer starting with something simple that we can measure — don't ship perfect before we know the workload."
- On incidents: "If the system is down for customers, don't wait to design the perfect fix; put a band-aid while we iterate."

Immediate next steps (today)
- Draft pairing task and share with candidate by EOD Friday. (Maya)
- Dana to ping references and ask kernel-specific questions by Mon.
- Leo to schedule 1-hr applied-ML pairing by next Wed.

Meta: tone and fit
- Candidate is collaborative and shipping-oriented. Will accelerate our reliability/playback efforts even if not a kernel expert day 1. Risk is manageable with the pairing trial.

Personal scribbles (notes-to-self)
- If trial goes well, mention potential mentorship with Priya (applied ML) and 1:1 with infra kernel lead.
- Consider bumping offer if candidate shows C++/CUDA competency in trial.

End of note.
